translations.title: Rhyme XCV: The Drop of Dew That Sleeps in the Lily
translations.text:
The drop of dew that sleeps within
the chalice of the whitest lily
is the crystal palace where
the happy spirit of purity lives.

He gives it mystery and poetry;
he lends it its soothing fragrance.
Alas for the flower if, kissed by light,
that pearl evaporates!
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Rhyme LXII: First a Trembling, Vague Glow
translations.text:
First a trembling, vague glow,
a line of restless light cutting across the sea;
then it sparks and grows and spreads
in a burning explosion of brightness.

The gleaming light is joy;
the fearful shadow is sorrow:
alas, in the dark night of my soul,
when will dawn come?
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Rhyme LXV: Night Came and I Found No Shelter
translations.text:
Night came and I found no shelter;
I was thirsty... I drank my tears;
I was hungry! I closed my swollen eyes
to sleep.

I was in a desert! Though the hoarse murmur
of the crowds reached my ears,
I was orphaned and poor... The world was
a desert... for me!
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Rhyme VI: Like the Breeze That Cools the Blood
translations.text:
Like the breeze that cools the blood
above the dark battlefield,
bearing perfumes and harmonies
through the wandering silence of night,

symbol of sorrow and tenderness
in the English bard's dreadful drama,
sweet Ophelia, her reason lost,
passes by gathering flowers and singing.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Rhyme LXXXVII: If Only I Were the Moon...
translations.text:
If only I were the moon,
if only I were the breeze,
if only I were the sun!

...

If only I were
the hour of twilight,
if only I were the moment
of your prayer!
If only I were part
of the prayer
you send alone
to God!

...

If only I were the moon,
if only I were the breeze,
if only I were the sun!...
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Rhyme XXXIX: Why Tell Me That?
translations.text:
Why tell me that? I know: she is changeable,
proud, vain, and capricious;
water will spring from barren rock
before feeling springs from her soul.

I know that in her heart, a nest of snakes,
there is not one fiber that answers love;
that she is a lifeless statue... but...
she is so beautiful!
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Rhyme IX: The Softly Sighing Breeze Kisses
translations.text:
The softly sighing breeze kisses
the gentle waves it playfully curls;
the sun kisses the cloud in the west
and colors it purple and gold;
the flame slips around the burning log
to kiss another flame,
and even the willow, bending under its weight,
returns a kiss to the river that kisses it.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Rhyme XXX: A Tear Rose in Her Eyes
translations.text:
A tear rose in her eyes,
and a word of forgiveness to my lips;
pride spoke, and she wiped away her tears,
and the word died upon my lips.

I take one road, she another;
but thinking of the love we shared,
I still say, “Why did I remain silent that day?”
And she will say, “Why did I not weep?”
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Rhyme LXXX: One Woman Has Poisoned My Soul
translations.text:
One woman has poisoned my soul,
another woman has poisoned my body;
neither of them came looking for me,
and I blame neither of them.

The world is round, and so the world turns.
If tomorrow, as it turns, this poison
poisons someone else, why blame me?
Can I give more than I was given?
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.
